response.sql: WITH order_counts AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.gender, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender), shares AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, CAST(number_of_orders AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(SUM(number_of_orders) OVER (PARTITION BY gender), 0) AS share FROM order_counts), compared AS (SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS gap_above_average FROM shares) SELECT customer_id, gender, number_of_orders, share, gap_above_average FROM compared WHERE gap_above_average > 0 ORDER BY (gap_above_average IS NULL), gap_above_average DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The average is across all customers with a recorded gender, including customers with zero orders. A share is undefined when that gender has no orders.

alternatives.interpretation: Compare each customer's share with the average share among customers of the same gender.
